references.text: The Gadites and Reubenites had previously promised to build enclosures for their livestock and cities for their children, which this verse confirms they intend to do.
The background of this verse is that the tribes of Reuben and Gad requested the land east of the Jordan because they had much livestock and the land was suitable for grazing.
Moses repeats the instruction that women, children, and livestock should remain in the cities east of the Jordan while the men cross over to fight.
Joshua reminds the Reubenites, Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh that their wives, children, and livestock must stay in the land Moses gave them east of the Jordan.
The fulfillment of the promise, where the tribes return to Gilead with their livestock and possessions after the conquest of Canaan was completed.
The list of cities built by the Gadites in Gilead, which were intended to house their families and livestock as mentioned in this verse.
